title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed by attackers against Thailand's Ministry of Finance between July 9 and 13, 2026, operating in unattended mode without human approval prompts. The agent automated post-exploitation tasks across the ministry's network. This represents a failure in the targeted systems' defensive perimeter, where attackers had already achieved initial access and then escalated their presence through automation rather than manual intervention.

The attack involved staging custom malware, exploit code for known vulnerabilities, webshells, and credential theft across multiple ministry servers. A custom implant called Hades handled command and control. The operation demonstrated detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal topology and systems, including its Hadoop infrastructure and mail systems. Detection required external security researchers to locate exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing attack artifacts, suggesting the ministry's own monitoring did not catch the autonomous agent's activity in real time.

Whether Hermes was purpose-built for this operation or repurposed from another context, and whether the attackers' use of an AI agent for post-exploitation represented a novel tactic or an incremental refinement of automated attack tools, is not established by the reporting.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance was targeted by attackers using Hermes, an autonomous AI agent operating in unattended mode without human approval prompts. Between July 9 and 13, 2026, researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing 585 files totaling 470 megabytes of attack code and stolen credentials. The operation also involved Hades, a custom implant built with Go that communicates over HTTPS. The attackers deployed exploit code for multiple known vulnerabilities, custom scripts targeting the ministry's Hadoop infrastructure and mail systems, and webshells across various ministry servers.

The attack campaign, attributed to a Chinese-speaking operator, involved detailed knowledge of the ministry's internal network topology and systems. Evidence included compromised session cookies from the ministry's ICT admin panel, hardcoded credentials for targeting Hadoop clusters, and scripts designed to exploit GlassFish application servers. Privilege escalation tools for both Linux and Windows were staged and ready for deployment. Thai authorities were notified on July 15, 2026, and the research was jointly conducted by Hunt.io and security researcher Bob Diachenko.
